# Transport manifest for #4974 item 3, cutover step 2 (docs/articles-generator-migration.md §5.2).
#
# One path or glob per line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
# Every path here is resolved relative to the repo root and must exist at resolve
# time, or the workflow fails loudly (a stale entry is a silent scope shrink, not
# a warning).
#
# Why a file instead of inline YAML: this set is the actual reviewable content of
# the transport — a diff to this file is a diff to what moves, independent of any
# workflow-syntax changes.
#
# WHY THIS IS NOT "scripts/lib/**": scripts/lib/ has 792 files on disk, and most
# of them are the job-crawler feature's per-employer parsers (job-parser.mjs,
# ats-clients/**, alerts/**, most of perf-sources/**, most of topic-sources/**,
# most of evidence/**, scheduler/winnerEvaluator.mjs) — unrelated to article
# generation and NOT part of the MOVE set in docs/articles-generator-migration.md
# §2. A blanket glob would ship ~730 irrelevant files into nanako's tree. The list
# below is the actual static-import transitive closure of the 7 entry points,
# computed by following relative import/export/require specifiers from each
# producer (regex-based, same limitation the doc's §1 methodology notes: dynamic
# `import()` behind a computed path is invisible to this and was checked by hand
# for the entries below — verified no entry uses one for its own lib tree).
#
# The doc's §2 prose describes this set by directory group ("discovery/**,
# scoring/**, topic-sources/**, evidence/**, scheduler/**, etc.") as a shorthand.
# Taken literally that shorthand is wrong for topic-sources/, evidence/, and
# scheduler/: each of those directories has files NOT reachable from any of the
# 7 entries (e.g. scripts/lib/scheduler/winnerEvaluator.mjs is only imported by
# scripts/tune-discovery-quota.mjs, a maintenance script outside this move; see
# the migration report for the full verification). This manifest lists the real
# closure, not the shorthand, on the theory that an explicit file list that has
# been checked beats a glob that has not.
#
# discovery/** and scoring/** ARE fully covered by every file the resolver found
# under those two directories, so they're expressed as globs; the rest are listed
# file-by-file because only part of each directory is in scope.

# --- The 7 MOVE entry points (docs §2, §4, §5.2) ---------------------------
# 5 named producers, the 7th undercounted producer (fix-faq-locales.mjs, §4/§6.5),
# and its paired helper (generate-journalist-image-catalog.mjs, §2: "the six
# producers themselves plus the two helper scripts one of them shells out to /
# is paired with"). NOTE: docs §5 step 2's own prose lists only 6 (producers +
# fix-faq-locales.mjs) and omits generate-journalist-image-catalog.mjs — that is
# a discrepancy between §2 (MOVE) and §5's summary sentence, not a hidden STAYS.
# Included here per §2's explicit disposition; flagged in the migration report
# for the doc author to reconcile.
scripts/create-article.mjs
scripts/generate-events-digest-article.mjs
scripts/generate-border-wait-ranking-article.mjs
scripts/publish-journalist-article.mjs
scripts/batch-add-faq-to-articles.mjs
scripts/fix-faq-locales.mjs
scripts/generate-journalist-image-catalog.mjs

# Added 2026-08-14 (see the `!rewired` block below for why this line is not
# optional). Single-pass decoder for TS string-literal source text, extracted by
# #5632/#5781 out of the `.replace()` chains that used to live inline. FOUR files
# already in this manifest import it — meta-field-regex.mjs, create-article.mjs,
# batch-add-faq-to-articles.mjs, article-topic-selector.mjs — and every one of
# those imports is a TOP-LEVEL `import`, so shipping them without this file is
# the "threw before main() on every invocation" failure documented at the bottom
# of this manifest, repeated verbatim. It is pure and imports nothing.
scripts/lib/unescape-ts-string.mjs

# --- !rewired: reachable by import, deliberately NOT moved -------------------
#
# Machine-readable form of the prose NOTE that used to live here alone. A
# decision that exists only as English fails nothing: `scripts/lib/unescape-ts-
# string.mjs` sat unlisted for a day with four listed importers, and the only
# thing standing between that and a dead generator was that nobody dispatched
# the transport. Every line below is checked by
# tests/mirror-transport-import-closure.test.ts, which requires each relative
# import of each listed file to be either LISTED above or `!rewired` here with a
# reason — so the next unlisted dependency is red in the PR that adds it, not in
# nanako at run time.
#
# Syntax: `# !rewired <repo-relative path> -- <why nanako does not need a copy>`
#
# !rewired scripts/lib/resolve-git-add-path.mjs -- Resolves a repo-relative path through a symlink to its real on-disk path for `git add`. Only exists because main's corpus paths are symlinks into packages/articles/. Docs §2: "STAYS main-shaped, but nanako needs its own equivalent... retire on the nanako side, note it explicitly so nobody ports it out of habit." nanako's generator/scripts/lib/corpus-paths.mjs (`resolveGitAddPaths`) is that equivalent, and its create-article.mjs already imports it instead.
# !rewired build-plugins/shared/articleSectionCore.mjs -- A symlink into packages/articles/engine/shared/, a tree nanako ALREADY mirrors via mirror-articles-engine.yml. Copying it would create a second, drifting copy of the section tuple; nanako's create-article.mjs imports `../../engine/shared/articleSectionCore.mjs` instead.
# !rewired build-plugins/shared/clauseTail.mjs -- Present on the corpus at host/shared/clauseTail.mjs, registered `identical` in nanako's scripts/ci/loop-sync-manifest.json; its create-article.mjs imports `../../host/shared/clauseTail.mjs`. A copy under generator/ would be a third one.
# !rewired data/border-wait-averages.json -- REWIRED, not transported (§5.3): regenerated here daily and fetched by nanako over HTTP from public/data/.
# !rewired scripts/lib/it-microcopy-guard.mjs -- nanako has its own generator/scripts/lib/it-microcopy-guard.mjs, registered in its manifest, and its create-article.mjs imports `./lib/it-microcopy-guard.mjs` from there. Transporting ours would overwrite a corpus-side file with a copy that has no reason to be fresher.
# !rewired scripts/lib/headline-selection-protocol.mjs -- nanako already has generator/scripts/lib/headline-selection-protocol.mjs: this file was copied FROM there (corpus PR #288, issue #188), it is registered `corpus-only` in nanako's scripts/ci/loop-sync-manifest.json, and its create-article.mjs imports `./lib/headline-selection-protocol.mjs` from there. Byte-identical to the corpus copy on the day it landed here; transporting ours would overwrite a corpus-side file with a copy that has no reason to be fresher — same disposition as it-microcopy-guard.mjs above.
# !rewired scripts/lib/cross-section-dedup.mjs -- nanako already has generator/scripts/lib/cross-section-dedup.mjs, copied FROM there in the same move (corpus PR #288, issue #251), registered `corpus-only` in nanako's scripts/ci/loop-sync-manifest.json, and its create-article.mjs imports `./lib/cross-section-dedup.mjs` from there. Same reason as the line above: the site copy exists because the site's create-article.mjs is a live twin, not because nanako lacks one.
# !rewired scripts/lib/slug-prompt-leak-guard.mjs -- nanako's equivalent is generator/scripts/lib/prompt-placeholder-guard.mjs (`sanitizePromptPlaceholders`, corpus #121), which its create-article.mjs already imports. Two implementations of "a prompt placeholder may not become a slug" is the drift this manifest exists to avoid; reconciling them is its own piece of work, not a transport.
# !rewired scripts/lib/slug-preservation-guard.mjs -- nanako's generator/scripts/lib/atomic-write-json.mjs is registered `adapted` precisely BECAUSE it drops this import: slug history is a job-crawler concern and nanako does not crawl jobs. Transporting it would also pull job-match-key.mjs, job-url-key.mjs and slug-history-journal.mjs behind it — the ~730-file widening the header of this file exists to prevent.

# --- Dependencies OUTSIDE scripts/ (added after the first transport) ---------
#
# The list above is the static-import closure computed WITHIN scripts/. Six of
# the moved files also import across the directory boundary — `../build-plugins/`,
# `../data/`, `../services/` — and those specifiers were never followed, so the
# first transport shipped code that could not load: these are top-level
# `import`s, so create-article.mjs threw before main() on every invocation in
# nanako. Found by running the transported code there rather than reading it.
#
# They land under generator/ at the same relative path they have here, which is
# what keeps the importing files' specifiers working with zero rewriting.
#
# NOT listed here, on purpose — the reachable ones now live in the `!rewired`
# block above, which is CHECKED rather than merely written down. The one that
# cannot: data/news-sitemap-whitelist.ts, VENDORED as .mjs on the nanako side
# (§5.3), deliberately a copy rather than a live dependency — no listed file
# imports it by a relative specifier from here, so it is invisible to the
# closure check and stays prose.
build-plugins/borderWaitData.ts
data/borderCrossings.ts
data/canton-url-slugs.json
data/municipalities.ts
services/borderCrossingSlug.ts
services/borderWaitFormat.ts
